---
title: Ideas worth keeping
subtitle: A small notebook for code and careful reading.
---

Good documentation gives an idea room to breathe. A clear heading, a comfortable
line, and a useful example help the reader find a way in.

## A small example

Code should feel at home beside the prose. A name like `entry.title` carries
the thought into a few lines you can run.

```{.python filename="notebook.py"}
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Entry:
    title: str
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()

note = Entry("The art of paying attention", ("reading",))
```

## Leave room for the reader

A useful page has a rhythm: a thought, an example, a pause. *Emphasis* gives
one phrase its place, and **strong text** makes a point easy to find again.

> A notebook is a place to think on paper, and a place to return to that thought.

| Piece | Purpose | Example |
|:------|:--------|:--------|
| A title | Name the idea | A reading notebook |
| A tag | Give it another home | `reading` |
| A link | Connect two thoughts | [Code and data](code.qmd) |
